title: Solid JSX Compilation: HTML Template Cloning & Surgical Node Setters

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Instead of building a toy model out of virtual blocks and comparing it to a blueprint, Solid creates a plastic mold (an HTML `<template>`) of the real elements. When a component appears, it stamps out a clone of the mold in one instant step, grabs pointers to only the dynamic text slots, and updates those exact text slots when data changes.
progressiveExplaining.junior: Solid's JSX compiler converts declarative JSX into native browser DOM operations without any runtime Virtual DOM. Static HTML elements are converted into `<template>` elements that are cloned using `cloneNode(true)` for maximum speed. Dynamic bindings (like `{count()}` or `class={active()}`) are compiled into surgical micro-effects that directly update element properties (`el.textContent = ...`, `el.className = ...`).
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, Solid JSX compilation achieves near-vanilla JavaScript performance by splitting templates into static and dynamic paths at compile time. Static subtrees are serialized into HTML strings passed to `template()`, which the browser parses natively into template DOM nodes. Dynamic holes are indexed by child/sibling traversal paths (`firstChild`, `nextSibling`), completely eliminating `document.createElement()` and `querySelector()` overhead during instantiation.

interviewGotchas.question: Why is `template.cloneNode(true)` faster than calling `document.createElement()` repeatedly?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of browser C++ DOM instantiation internals.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `cloneNode(true)` executes directly in the browser's optimized C++ engine layer in a single native operation. Calling `document.createElement()`, `setAttribute()`, and `appendChild()` repeatedly requires hundreds of cross-boundary JavaScript-to-C++ bindings calls, which incurs high overhead. Cloning a template HTML fragment is 2-5x faster.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not say that Solid uses `innerHTML` at runtime. Solid parses the HTML string into a `<template>` *once* at module load time, and only uses `cloneNode(true)` during component instantiation.

interviewGotchas.question: What does a Solid component return when called in JavaScript?
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: A Solid component returns **real, physical HTML DOM nodes** (e.g. an `HTMLDivElement` or `DocumentFragment`), *not* a Virtual DOM object, VNode, or Fiber descriptor.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: If you `console.log(<div />)` in SolidJS, you will see a live `HTMLDivElement` in the browser console, not a React element object `{ type: 'div', props: {} }`.
